title: A node's directory placement can contradict the status its own text asserts
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.1.2.4 is headed "a Directory of all Instances on Avalanche of the Allocation System Primitive with Instance status of `Active`." Its only child, A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.1.2.4.1 (Aave), then states: "The Avalanche Instances Directory of the Aave Protocol with `Completed` Status are stored herein."

Every sibling entry in the same directory — Base Morpho, Base Fluid, Base Aave, Arbitrum Fluid, Arbitrum Aave — uses `Active`. The Avalanche entry is the sole deviation, and it directly contradicts the parent it sits under.

This is worth recording because of how the Atlas encodes state. Instance status is expressed by **where** a subtree sits: successful Invocations move to the Active directory, failed ones are archived. Location-as-state removes the possibility of a status field disagreeing with reality — but only while the prose inside each node stays consistent with its placement, since these documents are maintained by hand.

Here they do not agree, and a reader cannot tell from the text alone whether the Avalanche Aave exposure is live or wound down. Either the entry was copied from a completed instance and the wording was not updated, or a genuinely completed instance was left in the Active tree.

The general lesson for anyone consuming Atlas data programmatically: derive status from tree position, and treat the descriptive sentence inside a node as commentary that may be stale.
description: Under the Avalanche Active Instances Directory, the Aave entry says it stores Instances with 'Completed' Status — so location-as-state and prose disagree about whether the exposure is live.
